Label the corner pads A (bottom-left) and C (top-right). Four pads are removed from the other 7, so there are C(7,4) = 35 ways in total.

Kevin can get home only if the 3 remaining non-corner pads, together with A and C, contain a path from A to C.

- The shortest path from A to C has 4 jumps and uses 3 intermediate pads. There are C(4,2) = 6 such monotone paths, and each corresponds to exactly one set of 3 kept pads.
- Any longer path has at least 6 jumps and uses at least 5 intermediate pads. That is more than the 3 available, so it is impossible.

So exactly 6 of the 35 removals leave Kevin a route, and the remaining 35 − 6 = 29 cut him off.

ANSWER: 29
